messages:
incident-bot: Pager duty triggered: INCIDENT p99_decode_latency spike on runtime-cluster-us-west starting 2026-03-15T22:33:09Z. Affected routes: /v1/generate-stream, /v1/chat/stream. p95: 380ms -> 720ms; p99: 820ms -> 2400ms. Paging team: eng-oncall rotation. Severity: Sev2. Link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streams/p99-decode :rotating_light:

samir: ack — I’m on it. pulling SLOs and customer list.

lee: I’m dialed in. assigning node shard group A3 as suspected.

marta: seeing streaming stalls correlate with decode tail events. p99 jumps coincide with kernel deployment yesterday 2026-03-14T02:10 UTC (trt8-flashattn-3.1). rolled to subset of infra.

dave: any active rollouts? kubectl shows rollout started 2026-03-14T02:09:47Z for runtime-kernel-daemonset v3.1.4 -> v3.1.5.

samir: grabbing traces. quick check: KV cache hits normal. memory pressure low. but decode kernel latency per-step shows a long tail on layers 11-13.

marta: stack traces point at flashattn kernel hot paths. CI shows new compiler flags in the v3.1.5 build: BUILD_FLAGS="--enable-flashattn --compiler-opts='-Ofast -march=native'" — suspect aggressive flags.

lee: good catch. can we revert kernel quickly?

samir: options: 1) rollback daemonset, 2) route streaming requests away from affected nodes, 3) pin customers to older model variant. starting rollback now.

samir: running:
```bash
kubectl -n runtime rollout undo daemonset/runtime-kernel-daemonset --to-revision=42
```

pagerduty-bot: Samir acknowledged the page. estimated ETA 20m for rollback.

marta: while rollback proceeds we should add routing rule to avoid A3 shard where the new kernel landed:
```bash
rdwctl route update --cluster us-west --avoid-shards "A3" --policy latency
```

dave: I’m seeing ~5% of nodes still reporting new kernel version. starting manual cordon+drain on leftovers.

lee: customer-impact quick numbers: ~14% of live streaming sessions saw at least one stall >1s in the last 30m. top impacted customer: acme-marketing (3% of their requests hit p99). CS notified.

samir: rollback finished on 6 nodes at 2026-03-15T22:45:10Z. early signal: p95 dropped from 720ms -> 420ms; p99 from 2400ms -> 980ms. still above SLO but improving.

marta: quick forensics: build artifacts show nvcc/clang flags differ between v3.1.4 and v3.1.5. v3.1.5 included -ffast-math/-Ofast in the kernel object for flashattn. correlating with TRT kernel changes.

dave: logs from one affected instance:
```text
[decode] layer 12 flash_attn kernel launch 0.002s -> 1.8s
cuda: stream stall detected
nvprof: context switch on stream 0
```

samir: creating short-lived mitigation: disable flashattn on streaming workers until kernel fix. applying per-deployment env var now:
```bash
kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/inference-worker DISABLE_FLASHATTN=true
```

lee: applied to canary. observing canary latencies stabilize.

ops-rotation: switching oncall to lee in 15m for handoff. please add notes.

marta: pinging @build-team — CI injected new default compiler flags on 2026-03-13 that likely caused the regression. recommend blocking -ffast-math/-Ofast for kernel builds until validation.

samir: incident summary note (to postmortem): suspected root cause: TRT/FlashAttention kernel variant built with aggressive compiler flags leading to tail latency regressions on certain sequence lengths and GPU microarchitectures. mitigations: rollback kernel, disable flashattn for streaming, patch CI to pin compiler flags, and run a perf sweep across seq len distribution.

dave: can we estimate total affected requests?

lee: approx 120k streaming requests in the 40m window, ~17k had at least one stall >500ms.

samir: drafting incident summary and notifying CS + account reps. retain trace TTL +24h for deeper analysis. cc: @sre for remediation playbook.

pagerduty-bot: Incident escalated to Sev2 -> owner: samir. next update in 10m.

lee: handoff notes pinned:
- rollback completed to v3.1.4 for runtime-kernel-daemonset
- DISABLE_FLASHATTN=true set for streaming workers
- CI rule added to block -ffast-math/-Ofast for kernel builds (temporary)
- follow-up: perf sweep on 2026-03-17, audit for compiler flag drift
- customer impact: ~14% sessions affected, top customers notified

marta: filing JIRA PERF-1248 to track kernel flag root cause and add test coverage across seq lengths and GPU types.

samir: closing page. monitoring 1hr for regression. thanks all :heart:
